raw_response:
I'm 54 this year, and I've been farming these same fields for 35 years. My family has six people — my wife, my son, my daughter-in-law, and two grandkids. My son works in a factory over in Handan and sends some money home every month, so that helps with cash, but my wife, my daughter-in-law, and me do most of the farm work ourselves. We have 64 mu of land. That's more than Old Wang down the road, but we still watch every yuan. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those technical leaflets from the extension office. I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted 22 mu last October with the regular improved variety from the seed station. Nothing fancy, but it's reliable. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu, and this year looks about the same so far. I'll topdress with urea at green-up, roughly half a bag per mu, and maybe another bit at jointing if the leaves look yellow. I'll irrigate two or three times before harvest — the well water is there but the electricity bill hurts, so I won't overdo it. I'll spray herbicide once in spring and watch for aphids. I can't spend too much on the wheat because I need cash for cotton planting right after.

For cotton, I'm planting 36 mu around April 20th, once the soil warms up. I use hybrid seed — costs about 80 yuan per mu, which is expensive, but my cousin said his did better against disease last year, so I'll stick with it. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as base, about one bag per mu, then topdress with urea at flowering. That comes to roughly 15 kg of nitrogen total per mu. I'll irrigate three times: at budding, flowering, and boll opening. I have to spray for bollworm and aphids three or four times — can't skip that or the whole year is wasted. For picking, I'll hire some women from the village because we can't handle 36 mu alone. Cotton prices go up and down like crazy, so I'm hoping for about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton, but I'm not counting on it. That's why I keep the wheat and maize — they're my safety net.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there's no time to waste — we plant summer maize on those same 22 mu within three or four days. I use hybrid seed, about 60 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, roughly 12 kg nitrogen equivalent, and if the plants look weak at jointing I'll side-dress a little more urea. Maize doesn't need as much water — maybe one or two irrigations, depending on rain. I'm hoping for 480 kg per mu, but if it's a dry summer I'll be happy with 400.

Then there's my 6 mu of stevia. I started growing it two years ago because my neighbor tried it and the buyer from Shijiazhuang pays decent money for dried leaves. It's a lot of work — you cut it multiple times and dry it carefully on tarps. I don't use much fertilizer, maybe 8 kg nitrogen per mu split over three times. It needs more water than cotton, so I'll irrigate five times. My daughter-in-law handles most of the cutting and drying because she's got patience for it. If I get 200 kg of dried leaves per mu, I'll be happy. It's a small gamble, but it brings in cash before the cotton is even picked.

All together — seed, fertilizer, pesticides, electricity for pumping, and hired labor — I'm looking at about 31,500 yuan in costs this year. My son sent 20,000 yuan home last year, and I'll use most of it, but I won't spend it all because we need cash in hand for the grandkids' school fees and if someone gets sick. So I keep my fertilizer a bit lower than what the rich business farms use. If cotton price is good, we'll have a decent year. If not, at least we'll have grain in the barn and stevia money in our pocket.
